## Summary

The new `CreateBackup` management RPC endpoint introduced in this PR streams the complete mint database to any caller who presents the correct protocol version header (`x-cdk-protocol-version: 1.0.0`). When the RPC server starts without a TLS directory (the default warned-about insecure mode), no authentication of any kind is enforced. The database contains all proof secrets (Y-values identifying spent ecash tokens), Lightning payment preimages from completed melt operations, all quote records, blind signatures, and full transaction history. Any attacker who can reach the RPC port — whether through a misconfigured firewall, a shared hosting environment, or a local network — can exfiltrate the entire database in a single streaming call.

PR #981 is titled "fix: update default mint settings" and its description states it "Updates the default value of `mint_rate_limit_proxy_trust` to `False`." The default value of `mint_rate_limit_proxy_trust` remains `True` after this PR merges. Every new nutshell deployment will still start with proxy-header trust enabled, leaving the rate-limit bypass vulnerability (XFF spoofing → unlimited request rate) fully intact. Security reviewers approving this PR based on its title and description would incorrectly conclude the insecure default has been corrected.

body:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | medium |
| **Target** | cashubtc/nuts |
| **Status** | theoretical |
| **Source PR** | [cashubtc/nuts#363](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts/pull/363) |
| **Specs** | NUT-29 |

## Summary

PR #363 adds a `timestamp` field to the NUT-29 `msg_to_sign` in order to prevent replay of quote-lookup signatures across different time periods. However, the specification only requires the *wallet* to include a valid signature over a message that incorporates the timestamp; it never places any normative requirement on the *mint* to validate that the timestamp is recent. Without a MUST-level staleness window, a valid signature obtained once is reusable indefinitely, rendering the timestamp's anti-replay purpose hollow.

The PR specifies that the NUT-29 `msg_to_sign` must include `mint_pubkey`, described as "the hex-encoded public key of the mint as defined in NUT-06." body:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | medium |
| **Target** | lescuer97/nutmix |
| **Status** | theoretical |
| **Specs** | NUT-05 |

## Summary

`CheckPayed` in `internal/lightning/lnbits.go` converts the LNBits fee field to `uint64` without applying `math.Abs`, unlike the `PayInvoice` function which correctly uses `math.Abs`. LNBits represents routing fees for outgoing payments as **negative** `int64` values (e.g., `-500` for a 500 msat fee). When `CheckPayed` is invoked on a PENDING melt quote — either via the error-recovery path in `Melt()` or the background CRON job `CheckPendingQuoteAndProofs` — the negative fee wraps around in uint64 arithmetic. This causes the change-calculation `totalExpent` to underflow to approximately `|fee_in_sats|`, making `overpaidFees` ≈ `proofs.Amount()`, and causing the mint to issue far more change than the user is entitled to.

body:
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Severity** | medium |
| **Target** | lescuer97/nutmix |
| **Status** | theoretical |
| **Specs** | NUT-05 |

## Summary

`PayInvoice` in `internal/lightning/lnbits.go` always sets `PaymentState = SETTLED` after a successful GET to `/api/v1/payments/{hash}`, regardless of whether the payment is actually settled. The `paymentStatus.Paid` boolean field — the primary indicator of payment confirmation — is never checked. If LNBits returns `paid: false, pending: true` (in-flight payment), `PayInvoice` still reports `SETTLED` to the mint. The mint then marks the melt quote as PAID, burns user proofs as SPENT, and issues change. If the in-flight payment subsequently fails, the mint has permanently spent the proofs and the LNBits wallet recredits the funds — causing mint financial loss.

## Summary

The `dart-publish.yml` workflow installs the `cross` cross-compilation tool directly from the HEAD of the `cross-rs/cross` default branch using `cargo install cross --git https://github.com/cross-rs/cross` without specifying a commit hash or a version tag. Any commit pushed to that repository's default branch — including a malicious one introduced via supply-chain compromise of `cross-rs/cross` — would be compiled and executed inside the Android build runners. Those runners have access to all GitHub Actions secrets exposed to the job, the repository contents, and the Cargo registry credentials, enabling secret exfiltration and artifact poisoning.
